bundles.publication_markdown:
This structure supplies an abstract height formalism. Its 15 fields name curves, point types, degree subsets, three real functions, the tripod, and compactly bounded subsets. It also supplies two degree-filter laws and a proof that the tripod is hyperbolic. These fields describe the intended geometric interpretation. The structure itself does not construct number fields, curves, divisors, heights, or local bounding domains. Source context: [GenEll], Definition 1.2(i)–(ii), p. 5; Example 1.3(i)–(ii), pp. 5–6; Proposition 1.4(iii), p. 6; Definition 1.5(iii)–(iv), p. 8; Theorem 2.1(i)–(ii), p. 11.

**Source connection**

Mochizuki reviews these objects in §1 of [GenEll] and uses them in Theorem 2.1, p. 11. The source code selects an interface sufficient to state that theorem.

**Limits of the definition supplier**

Curve and Pt are abstract types. Their geometric meanings come from the interpretation, not the bare types.

Hyperbolic and DivisorFree are predicates supplied by the interface.

The two degree-filter equations are explicit Lean interface laws. The paper defines degree subsets by fields and set difference.

CBS and cbsSet do not carry local domains or a named finite set Σ. The intended support condition is implicit in the choice of CBS.

No StatementI or StatementII theorem is part of the selected structure command.

**Original papers**

[Arithmetic Elliptic Curves in General Position](https://www.kurims.kyoto-u.ac.jp/~motizuki/Arithmetic%20Elliptic%20Curves%20in%20General%20Position.pdf)

[Inter-universal Teichmüller Theory IV: Log-volume Computations and Set-theoretic Foundations](https://www.kurims.kyoto-u.ac.jp/~motizuki/Inter-universal%20Teichmuller%20Theory%20IV.pdf)

For local height data L, heightEq(q) sums the terms at bad places with residue characteristic q, then divides by L.deg. The function heightOther(a,b) sums the terms whose residue characteristics differ from both a and b, with the same denominator. Each term is hv(v)·f(v)·log(p(v)). These formulas partition the globally normalized height from IUT IV, p. 44. Source context: IUT IV, Corollary 2.2(i), p. 41; proof of Corollary 2.2(ii), total-height paragraph on p. 44, (P5) on p. 46, and the first comparison on p. 47; Theorem 1.10, p. 23.

**Source connection**

Corollary 2.2(i), p. 41 separates all nonarchimedean primes from those away from 2. Condition (P5), p. 46 selects bad places away from 2l. Theorem 1.10, p. 23 defines its q-divisor on those selected bad places.

**Limits of the definition supplier**

heightOther(2,l) is identified with the theorem input log(q) only by the supplied thetaData equality. The generic sum definition alone proves no such geometric identification.

heightEq(q) keeps the global denominator deg. It is not Definition 1.9(ii)’s normalized E-degree, whose denominator sums local degrees over E.

The support sets can be empty. If a=b, the two exclusions coincide; a three-part decomposition requires a≠b.

The pilot quantity |log(q-underlined-underlined)| is log(q)/(2l), as stated in Theorem 1.10, p. 23. It must not be equated directly with heightOther(2,l).

> $h\overset{\mathrm{def}}{=}\log(\mathfrak q^{\forall})=\frac{1}{[F:\mathbb Q]}\cdot\sum_{v\in\mathbb V(F)^{\mathrm{non}}}h_v\cdot f_v\cdot\log(p_v)$

— that is to say, $h_v=0$ for those $v$ at which $E_F$ has good reduction; $h_v\in\mathbb N_{\geq1}$ is the local height of $E_F$ [cf. [GenEll], Definition 3.3] for those $v$ at which $E_F$ has bad multiplicative reduction.

— Inter-universal Teichmüller Theory IV: Log-volume Computations and Set-theoretic Foundations, §2, proof of Corollary 2.2(ii), paragraph beginning “Next, let us write”, printed pp. 44.

> We shall refer to the positive integer $v_K(q_E)\in\mathbb Z_{>0}$ as the local height of $E$ [or $E_K$].

— Arithmetic Elliptic Curves in General Position, §3, Definition 3.3, printed pp. 15.

> (P5) if we write $\mathbb V_{\mathrm{mod}}^{\mathrm{bad}}$ for the set of nonarchimedean valuations $\in\mathbb V_{\mathrm{mod}}\overset{\mathrm{def}}{=}\mathbb V(F_{\mathrm{mod}})$ that do not divide $2l$ and at which $E_F$ has bad multiplicative reduction, then $\mathbb V_{\mathrm{mod}}^{\mathrm{bad}}\neq\emptyset$.

[…] (P6) the image of the outer homomorphism $\operatorname{Gal}(\overline{\mathbb Q}/F)\to GL_2(\mathbb F_l)$ determined by the $l$-torsion points of $E_F$ contains the subgroup $SL_2(\mathbb F_l)\subseteq GL_2(\mathbb F_l)$.

Indeed, since, by (P5), $E_F$ has bad multiplicative reduction at some valuation $\in\mathbb V_{\mathrm{mod}}^{\mathrm{bad}}\neq\emptyset$, (P6) follows formally from (P2), (P4), and [GenEll], Lemma 3.1, (iii) [cf. the proof of the final portion of [GenEll], Theorem 3.8].

— Inter-universal Teichmüller Theory IV: Log-volume Computations and Set-theoretic Foundations, §2, proof of Corollary 2.2(ii), (P5), (P6) and sentence after (P6), printed pp. 46.

> $\frac16\cdot\log(\mathfrak q)\leq\frac16\cdot\log(\mathfrak q^{\nmid2})\leq\frac16\cdot\log(\mathfrak q^{\forall})\leq(1+\epsilon_E)\cdot(\operatorname{log\text{-}diff}_X(x_E)+\operatorname{log\text{-}cond}_D(x_E))+C_{\mathcal K}$

— where we write

$\epsilon_E\overset{\mathrm{def}}{=}(60\delta)^2\cdot\frac{\log(2\delta\cdot(\log(\mathfrak q^{\forall})))}{(\log(\mathfrak q^{\forall}))^{1/2}}$.

— Inter-universal Teichmüller Theory IV: Log-volume Computations and Set-theoretic Foundations, §2, Corollary 2.2(ii), condition (C2) and definition of ε_E, printed pp. 42.

> If $\mathfrak a\in\operatorname{ADiv}_{\mathbb R}(F)$, then we shall refer to

$$\underline{\deg}(\mathfrak a)\overset{\mathrm{def}}{=}\frac{1}{[F:\mathbb Q]}\cdot\deg_F(\mathfrak a)$$

as the normalized degree of $\mathfrak a$. Thus, for any finite extension $K$ of $F$, we have

$$\underline{\deg}(\mathfrak a|_K)=\underline{\deg}(\mathfrak a)$$

— where we write $\underline{\deg}(\mathfrak a|_K)$ for the normalized degree of the pull-back $\mathfrak a|_K\in\operatorname{ADiv}_{\mathbb R}(K)$ [defined in the evident fashion] of $\mathfrak a$ to $K$.

— Inter-universal Teichmüller Theory IV: Log-volume Computations and Set-theoretic Foundations, §1, Definition 1.9(i), sentence defining normalized degree and pullback equality, printed pp. 21, 22.

> Let $v_{\mathbb Q}\in\mathbb V_{\mathbb Q}\overset{\mathrm{def}}{=}\mathbb V(\mathbb Q)$, $E\subseteq\mathbb V(F)$ a nonempty set of elements lying over $v_{\mathbb Q}$. If $\mathfrak a=\sum_{v\in\mathbb V(F)}c_v\cdot v\in\operatorname{ADiv}_{\mathbb R}(F)$, then we shall write

$$\mathfrak a_E\overset{\mathrm{def}}{=}\sum_{v\in E}c_v\cdot v\in\operatorname{ADiv}_{\mathbb R}(F);\qquad\underline{\deg}_E(\mathfrak a)\overset{\mathrm{def}}{=}\frac{\deg(\mathfrak a_E)}{\sum_{v\in E}[F_v:\mathbb Q_{v_{\mathbb Q}}]}$$

for the portion of $\mathfrak a$ supported in $E$ and the “normalized $E$-degree” of $\mathfrak a$, respectively.

— Inter-universal Teichmüller Theory IV: Log-volume Computations and Set-theoretic Foundations, §1, Definition 1.9(ii), opening through the definition of normalized E-degree, printed pp. 22.

> Here, we observe that the various “$\log(q_{(-)})$”’s are independent of the choice of $F_{\square}$, and that the quantity “$\lvert\log(\underline{\underline q})\rvert\in\mathbb R_{>0}$” defined in [IUTchIII], Corollary 3.12, is equal to $\frac{1}{2l}\cdot\log(q)\in\mathbb R$ [cf. the definition of “$\underline q_{\underline v}$” in [IUTchI], Example 3.2, (iv)].

— Inter-universal Teichmüller Theory IV: Log-volume Computations and Set-theoretic Foundations, §1, Theorem 1.10 statement, sentence beginning “Here, we observe”, printed pp. 23.

The function epsilonE(δ,h) returns (60δ)²·log(2δh)/sqrt(h). For the positive height h=log(q^∀), this is the ε_E in Corollary 2.2(ii), p. 42. The function deltaBound(d) returns 552960d, which equals 2¹²·3³·5·d. Corollary 2.2(ii) uses this δ, and its proof bounds [F:Q] by δ on p. 44. Source formulas: IUT IV, Corollary 2.2(ii), opening and (C2), p. 42. The field-degree bound occurs in its proof, p. 44. The ε_E argument occurs on p. 47.

**Limits of the definition supplier**

The Lean definitions are total on their formal domains. The paper uses positive d and positive height h under its geometric hypotheses.

The equality 2¹²·3³·5=552960 is arithmetic. It does not establish the geometric degree bound; localData_deg_le supplies that bound.

The numeric definitions alone establish neither ε_E≤1 nor the C2 inequality.

> Fix a collection of initial $\Theta$-data as in [IUTchI], Definition 3.1. Suppose that we are in the situation of [IUTchIII], Corollary 3.12, and that the elliptic curve $E_F$ has good reduction at every valuation $\in\mathbb V(F)^{\mathrm{good}}\cap\mathbb V(F)^{\mathrm{non}}$ that does not divide $2l$. In the notation of [IUTchI], Definition 3.1, let us write $d_{\mathrm{mod}}\overset{\mathrm{def}}{=}[F_{\mathrm{mod}}:\mathbb Q]$, $(1\leq)\ e_{\mathrm{mod}}\ (\leq d_{\mathrm{mod}})$ for the maximal ramification index of $F_{\mathrm{mod}}$ [i.e., of valuations $\in\mathbb V_{\mathrm{mod}}^{\mathrm{non}}$] over $\mathbb Q$, $d_{\mathrm{mod}}^*\overset{\mathrm{def}}{=}2^{12}\cdot3^3\cdot5\cdot d_{\mathrm{mod}}$, $e_{\mathrm{mod}}^*\overset{\mathrm{def}}{=}2^{12}\cdot3^3\cdot5\cdot e_{\mathrm{mod}}\ (\leq d_{\mathrm{mod}}^*)$, and

for the “tripodal” intermediate field obtained from $F_{\mathrm{mod}}$ by adjoining the fields of definition of the $2$-torsion points of any model of $E_F\times_F\overline F$ over $F_{\mathrm{mod}}$ [cf. Proposition 1.8, (ii), (iii)].
